h1: Oil Tank Replacement and Removal in Mount Pearl, NL
heroSub: Mount Pearl's 1970s and 80s subdivisions are running out of tank tag all at once. We replace, remove and upgrade oil tanks across the city, with a free written estimate before a wrench comes out.
introHtml:
Mount Pearl is St. John's biggest neighbour, and most of it was built in one long push through the 1970s and 80s. The streets off Park Avenue, Commonwealth Avenue, Ruth Avenue and Old Placentia Road went up with an oil furnace in the basement and a steel tank on the side of the house, and plenty of those homes still heat that way. An outdoor single-wall steel tank is only tagged for 10 to 20 years, so if yours is the original or a replacement from the 2000s, the HOST tag is either done or close to it.

Harbour Tank Co handles oil tank replacement, tank removal and fibreglass upgrades across Mount Pearl, from Topsail Road down to Old Placentia Road and out to the Paradise line. The crew is licensed and insured, every job starts with a free written estimate, and there's a 24/7 line for the day the oil truck pulls away without filling you. Call (709) 800-3117, or keep reading for what the job involves and what it costs.

sections.heading: Why so many Mount Pearl tanks are expiring at once
sections.html:
Mount Pearl grew fast. Whole subdivisions off Park Avenue, Smallwood Drive and Old Placentia Road went up within a few years of each other, and nearly every house got an oil furnace and a steel tank against the side wall or out back. Furnaces and tanks that went in together tend to wear out together, which is why one street can see three or four tank swaps in the same winter.

Under the province's heating oil tank rules, a steel tank only gets a set number of years before it has to come out, no matter how solid it looks from the driveway. Outdoors and single wall, that's 10 to 20 years depending on the gauge of the steel and where the outlet is. Indoors it's 15 to 25. The date is stamped on the metal HOST tag in month and year form, so a tag reading 7-2028 means no oil after the end of July 2028.

Steel gets a hard life on the Avalon. Wet snow, freeze and thaw and damp salt air rust the outside, while condensation eats the inside where you can't see it. If you bought in Mount Pearl and never read the tag, go look today. If it's expired or within a year of it, book a replacement before the cold sets in and everyone else on the street is calling too.

sections.heading: What a Mount Pearl tank job costs and how it goes
sections.html:
Most tank companies in town won't put a number on their website. We'd rather you know what you're comparing before we come out. These are installed prices in Canadian dollars, and every one of them includes taking the old tank away.

  • 200-gallon painted steel tank, installed: $3,200, outside or inside
  • Fibreglass tank, installed: $3,850, outside or inside
  • Roth double-containment tank, installed inside: $3,850
  • 100-gallon steel tank, installed: $3,100, common in homes that keep oil as heat pump backup
  • Removal and disposal only, outdoor tank: $500. Basement and indoor removals are quoted case by case.

The job itself usually fits in a single visit. We pump any remaining oil out of the old tank, disconnect the lines and set the new tank on a level base. Then we connect it, bleed the line and fire the furnace, and the installer's licensed inspector tags and registers the new system so your supplier is clear to deliver. The old tank goes on our truck, and you get the paperwork your insurer or oil company may ask for.

Your written estimate spells out the tank, the labour, the disposal and the registration, so there's nothing to argue about when the truck shows up. If you're weighing steel against fibreglass, our fibreglass upgrade page lays out the trade-offs and our cost guide explains what moves the price up or down.

sections.heading: Refused delivery or a leak in Mount Pearl: what to do now
sections.html:
The call usually comes in the coldest week of the year. The oil truck pulls up on Park Avenue, the driver reads the tag, sees it's expired or spots a drip, and leaves without filling. He's not being difficult. The regulations say oil can't be delivered to a tank without a valid tag, and the driver has to report what he found to you and to the province.

Call our 24/7 emergency line at (709) 800-3117 any hour and tell us where you are in Mount Pearl and what the driver said. We'll get a crew scheduled as fast as we can, tell you whether the tank is safe to leave as it is until we get there, and talk through how to keep the house warm in the meantime. Any after-hours premium varies by contractor, and it'll be in writing before we start.

If the tank is leaking, don't patch it, don't move it and don't hose the spot down. Keep people and pets away and call. Oil that gets into a ditch in Mount Pearl heads for the Waterford River, and once a tank has leaked the province gives you 10 days to get it emptied and out, plus 30 days for cleanup, so speed matters. A small drip caught today is a tank swap, while a leak that soaks in beside the foundation is a much bigger bill.

faq.q: The oil company refused delivery at my Mount Pearl house. How fast can you get here?
faq.a: Call (709) 800-3117 and we'll give you a real answer for your address, not a guess. Mount Pearl is only minutes from St. John's along Topsail Road or the Team Gushue Highway, so it's one of the quickest areas for us to reach. Expired-tag refusals go to the front of the line in winter, and once the new tank is tagged you can call your supplier and rebook the delivery.

faq.q: How much does an oil tank replacement cost in Mount Pearl?
faq.a: A 200-gallon painted steel tank installed is $3,200 and a fibreglass tank is $3,850, and both prices include removing the old tank. Steel costs less up front, while fibreglass won't rust through and carries a far longer tag, which matters for an outdoor tank in a Newfoundland winter. We'll put both in your written estimate so you can decide, and our cost guide covers what changes the price.

faq.q: We're selling our house in Mount Pearl. Does the tank tag matter?
faq.a: It does. The buyer's insurer will usually want proof the tank is registered and in date, and lawyers and realtors ask for it too, often right before closing. If your tag has expired or has less than a year left, replacing it before you list saves a last-minute price cut. If you're the buyer, read the tag during the inspection and get a free written estimate so you can negotiate it.

faq.q: I've switched to a heat pump. Can you just take the old oil tank away?
faq.a: Yes, and that's a growing share of our Mount Pearl calls. Removing an outdoor tank is $500, while basement tanks are quoted case by case because getting them out the door is the hard part. Once a tank is disconnected the province gives you 30 days to have it emptied, removed and the lines capped, so don't leave it sitting, and the main oil-to-heat-pump rebates have closed to new applicants, so plan on this being your own cost. See our tank removal page for how it works.
